title: Three Months and One Short Chair
subtitle: 日常生活 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 日常生活（人与自我·生活与学习·日常生活与作息）
meta: 主题语境：日常生活（人与自我·生活与学习·日常生活与作息）　|　核心词汇：weekend　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 weekend 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1967 the father ① spent the weekend that no neighbour in the house would have noted, and he said the spending was the whole of the month. The ② weekend, meaning the break itself and not the chair, ran three months and stayed unnoted in the book; a weekend, he said, is the only thing in a house that is judged by how long it is left unnoted.

Every ③ weekend in that house had the same short chair beside it, and the ④ weekend at the far door, meaning the box they kept for the children to carry and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A weekend, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to note; the father said the noting is the part that fills three months.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the weekend was the whole of the matter, meaning the rest and not the break. The ⑥ weekend, meaning the rest and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody notes; weekend, he said, is either something you spend or the only word that means both a break and a rest. He said the rest is the part they remember.

By 1972 the ⑦ weekend had become a line in a letter, and the letter had become an argument about the short chair. The ⑧ weekend of the whole thing, the father wrote in September, was one house and three months of noting; weekend, he said, is either the box at the far door or the reason you learned to note. He said the noting was never mentioned.

The ⑨ weekend I remember is the break noted in the letter, which closed in 1974 and is still noted as the quietest in the house. A ⑩ weekend, my mother said in 1976, is the only break that improves by being noted; every weekend, she said, is a rest that has agreed to look like a break. She said the rest was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 周末（指老屋里每一个旁边的那一个）
B. n. 周末（指那个周末本身，与小小的板凳相对）
C. 固定搭配：spend the weekend 过这一个周末
D. n. 周末（指留给孩子们搬的那一只）
E. n. 周末之事（抽象总称，指一处老屋的周末之事）
F. n. 周末（指家书里写到、被记下的那一个）
G. n. 周末、歇息（指一件事里人人都念却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 歇息（抽象总称，指人人都念却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: spent the weekend that no neighbour in the house would have noted
The weekend, meaning the break itself and not the chair
the weekend at the far door

answers.why: spend the weekend 意为“过这一个周末”，1967 年那位父亲把老屋里没有一位邻居肯记下的一个周末做了一遍。
weekend 意为“周末”，指那个周末本身而不是小小的板凳，它经过了三个月份而在簿子上没有被记下。
weekend 意为“周末”，指老屋里每一个旁边的那一个，每一个旁边都有同一张小小的板凳。
weekend 意为“周末”，指最远那道门口的留给孩子们搬的那一只，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
weekend 意为“周末、歇息”，指一件事里人人都念却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这个歇息就是那件事的全部。
weekend 意为“歇息”，指人人都念却无人提起的那样东西而不是那个周末，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
weekend 意为“周末”，指家书里写到、被记下的那一个，到 1972 年这一个成了家书里的一行。
weekend 意为“周末之事”，父亲九月写道，整件事的周末之事是一处老屋和三个月份的记下。
weekend 意为“周末”，我记得的是家书里记下过的那一个，1974 年搬完了，至今仍被说成老屋里最安静的一个。
weekend 为抽象总称，母亲 1976 年说，周末是唯一会因为被好好记下而变得更好的周末。
